chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Yahya ibn al-Mubarik, from Abdillah ibn Jabala, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said:

I said to him, 'May I be your ransom, I had a sheep that I had fattened to sacrifice with it. When I took it and laid it down, it looked at me, so I felt mercy for it and was tender towards it. Then I slaughtered it.' He said to me, 'I would not like for you to do that; do not raise one of these and then slaughter it.'

key_terms.كَبْشٌ: A male sheep, specifically used here for sacrifice
key_terms.لِأُضَحِّيَ بِهِ: To sacrifice it (for Eid al-Adha or general udhiyah)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on fattening animals before slaughtering them for sacrifice?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) critiques the practice of fattening animals for sacrifice, noting that the owner's resulting emotional attachment transforms the ritual slaughter into a more poignant act of killing a beloved creature. This reflects the Shia emphasis on *adab* (etiquette) and spiritual mindfulness (*khushu*) in worship, suggesting that excessive care can introduce sentimental distraction from the solemnity of the act. The teaching encourages believers to maintain a balance between kindness and the ritualistic detachment required for *udhiyah*.
